verdict.rationale: Microsoft Graph documents a broad first-party mail API. It covers drafting, reading, replying, forwarding, sending and deleting messages, plus attachments, Inbox rules, categories, flags and importance, automatic replies and working hours, search, sync and change notifications. That is a large share of what users do in the UI. However, no evidence claims or shows full UI-to-API parity, and the pack does not address UI-only features. Missing for 10: an explicit parity statement or feature-by-feature coverage of UI capabilities, and independent hands-on confirmation that no UI actions are missing from the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Draft, read, reply, forward, send, update, or delete messages
Add, get, or delete attachments of a message
Get or update a user's automatic reply, locale, time zone, or working hours
Use Inbox rules to automate actions such as forwarding specific incoming messages
app users can change the importance of a message (or event or task), or flag a message for follow-up
Synchronize messages or mail folder hierarchy
